feature_policy: Operational event-time replay assumption: flight records are available at flightdate + 3 days. At a reference midnight, use flightdate <= reference_date - 3 days. This is not a reconstruction of historical BTS public-release availability.
label_policy: Keep each original SQL window (reference_date, reference_date+7 days] and all original NULL, aggregation and threshold semantics. Full-window label availability is inclusive end date + 3 days under the operational replay assumption.
sampling_policy: Rank real historical entity/reference pairs per original question; allocate one unused bound-SQL unit per parent per round, up to 10 rounds. Parent order and candidate order are hashed with seed 42. Allocate before labels; no outcome balancing or replacement after rejection.
head_training_policy: Train on support/train, select on support/validation, and keep original qa/test as the current main test. Revised support/test is reserved for separate final evaluation, never per-query adaptation.

premise_rules.RDB_FIN_952: Require at least one historically visible flight with distance >= 2500 miles, consistent with the dataset's stated long-haul definition.
premise_rules.RDB_FIN_999: Keep original ATL anchor to preserve the major-hub premise without inventing a hub category for other airports; only shift time.

timing_limitations: Known noncancelled flight completion durations fit inside the 3-day lag even after adding a 24-hour clock buffer. Cancellation/unfinished-diversion resolution, delay-cause reporting, correction histories and actual monthly publication times are not timestamped; their availability within this lag is an explicit assumption.
test_support_policy: Final temporal evaluation instances only; not adaptation data. Existing qa/test remains the current experiment cohort.
